msk1.review: I took CSE422 (Probabilistic Modeling and Simulation) with MSK1 last semester. The course is heavily focused on the mathematical and theoretical aspects of probabilistic modeling, with some practical applications through coding assignments and a final project. I'd say it was about 80% math, 15% theory, and 5% coding. At the beginning of the course, we reviewed mathematical fundamentals including combinatorics, set theory, derivation, and integration. This was followed by in-depth topics such as probability theory, random variables, and we concluded with queuing theory. All the class notes and course contents are available on his webpage. I don't recommend this course unless you're really into math.
